In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the mosquitto_ctrl utility would crash if attempting to interact with a hostile broker and the broker sent a non-string "error" value.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, using the mosquitto_ctrl utility in interactive shell mode to interact with a malicious server could result in a crash of the utility if the server sent a hostile response.

A flaw was found in lldpd. The service fails to verify that Link Layer Discovery Protocol - Media Endpoint Discovery (LLDP-MED) location records received from network neighbors match their declared lengths. An adjacent attacker on the local network can exploit this flaw by sending crafted packets, causing client applications using the liblldpctl library to read past buffer boundaries when parsing location data. This issue can lead to an information disclosure of adjacent process memory.

MISP (Malware Information Sharing Platform) contains an authorization bypass in the SharingGroup model's captureSGExisting method. The authorization check used a logical AND condition that effectively exempted users with the sync permission (perm_sync) from the membership verification. Specifically, the original condition 'if (!checkIfAuthorised(...) && !perm_sync) return false' meant that any user holding the sync role would pass the check regardless of whether they were actually a member of the target sharing group.

A sync user who knows or can discover the UUID of a non-local sharing group could exploit this flaw through the /sharing_groups/add endpoint or by embedding a SharingGroup object in pushed sync data. The attacker could rewrite the sharing group record to add their own organisation as a member or insert an all_orgs server entry for their MISP instance, thereby gaining read access to all events contained in that group. This exposes threat intelligence data that was intended to be restricted to the group's legitimate members.

The vulnerability requires an authenticated account with the sync role and knowledge of a valid sharing group UUID. No user interaction is required. The impact is unauthorized disclosure of shared threat intelligence events and limited integrity modification of the sharing group record.

nVision sends user's token via query parameters of GET requests. An attacker who obtains valid token can gain access to the victim's account and perform actions on their behalf.


This issue was fixed in version 18.

The Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.0.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit succeeds even though wp_kses is applied on save, because the XSS is manufactured post-sanitization by the plugin's regex pass: kses-permitted tags such as <a title> and <code> carry the attacker's marker and terminator strings intact into the rendered HTML buffer, where the plugin's own replacement then corrupts the document structure.

The Delivery & Pickup Date Time for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.3.90. This is due to a nonce-only settings AJAX handler that stores an attribute-breaking value and an administrator settings template that outputs it without HTML attribute escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.

The WP Maps – Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, Mapbox, Store Locator with Search, Filters & Listings plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'csv_columns' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content/excerpt (REST wp/v2/posts) → stored in post_content/post_excerpt' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor's entity-encoded payload survives save-time wp_kses filtering verbatim and is only decoded into raw script tags at render time via html_entity_decode(), meaning the injected script executes for every visitor — including authenticated Administrators — once an Editor publishes the post through the standard Contributor workflow.
Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. Exploitation could lead to arbitrary command execution with root privileges on the appliance.

In specific versions of Octopus Tentacle, Tentacle fails to unset registration credentials as environment variables, resulting in deployment scripts potentially having the ability to read those credentials.

The Check & Log Email – Easy Email Testing & Mail logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires an administrator to approve the comment carrying the shortcode payload, and the target page must render the core Latest Comments block, which passes comment author names through do_shortcode via the_content.

The Custom Twitter Feeds – A Tweets Widget or X Feed Widget plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'atts (JSON object, specifically the inner `feed` key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is first stored in the wp_ctf_feed_caches database table and later written into the ctf_cron_report WordPress option by the scheduled ctf_feed_update cron job, meaning execution is deferred until the cron runs and an administrator subsequently loads the Support page.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

The DataPress (Dataverse Integration) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.97 via the 'src' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Exploitation requires WP_DEBUG to be defined as true on the target site — not the default on production, but commonly enabled on staging, development, and misconfigured production environments.

The HTML Forms – Simple WordPress Forms Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'arbitrary POST parameter NAME (the array key, not the value)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Script execution does not require the Screen Options panel to be opened — injected attributes on the hidden-column checkboxes fire on page load as soon as the Submissions tab is rendered.

The Dokan: AI Powered WooCommerce Multivendor Marketplace Solution – Build Your Own Amazon, eBay, Etsy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.3. The vulnerability exists because the `matches_mcp_endpoint()` function applies an unanchored regular expression (`#/(?:woocommerce|dokan)/mcp(?:/|$)#`) against the entire `REQUEST_URI` including the query string, meaning any request that contains the literal substring `/dokan/mcp/` or `/woocommerce/mcp/` anywhere in its URI — including inside a query parameter value — is incorrectly treated as a trusted internal MCP context, causing `scope_product_permissions()` to unconditionally return `true` on WooCommerce's `woocommerce_rest_check_permissions` filter regardless of whether the caller is authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read full authenticated WooCommerce REST product records for any published product — including private underscore-prefixed meta, purchase notes, downloadable file URLs for paid digital products, catalog-hidden products, and edit-context representations — across the `/wc/v1`, `/wc/v2`, `/wc/v3`, and `/wc-analytics` REST namespaces. The bypass is triggered by appending a query parameter whose value contains the literal string `/dokan/mcp/` to any WooCommerce REST product endpoint (e.g., `/wp-json/wc/v3/products/{id}?x=/dokan/mcp/`); note that percent-encoding the slashes prevents the bypass, as the unencoded literal slash characters are required for the regex to match.

The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 via the `draft_post()` function. This is due to the function storing the `post_content` parameter via `wp_insert_post()` without the protected-shortcode allow-list check that was introduced in 4.3.14 for the sibling `submit_post()` handler — a gap that `wp_kses` filtering does not close, as it strips only HTML tags while leaving shortcode text such as `[wpuf-registration role="editor"]` intact. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to embed a registration shortcode in a post and cause any site visitor who subsequently registers through the rendered form to receive Editor-level access. The render-time `wpuf_modify_shortcodes` filter that is designed to neutralize protected shortcodes provides no protection here because posts created via the `wpuf_draft_post` AJAX endpoint carry no `_edit_last` post meta, causing the filter to return the content unchanged and allowing the shortcode to render and execute fully.

The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' merge-tag of the [ghr] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 4.10 The post_title replacement is registered with 'nested' => true, so the nested branch of Replacements::do_replacement() returns the merge value through tackle_replacements() without passing it through escape_merge_tags()/escape_shortcodes(); the callback single_post() calls html_entity_decode(get_the_title(), ENT_QUOTES), converting the entity-encoded text that wp_filter_kses leaves intact on a Contributor's post title back into raw HTML, which is then emitted into the rendered post. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to missing authorization to Unauthorized Social App Data Modification in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 This is due to missing authentication, nonce, and capability checks in the `standardFSApp()` function, which is registered on the `wp` action hook and executes on every frontend page load without any login or permission verification. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to insert arbitrary social network app records into the database, or overwrite the OAuth `client_id` and `client_secret` of existing social network connections, by supplying attacker-controlled values via the `fsp_app_redirect` and `app` GET parameters. An attacker can target a specific existing social app record for credential overwrite by supplying matching `social_network` and `slug` values, requiring no knowledge of internal record IDs, which disrupts scheduled social media posts and forces administrators to re-authenticate their connected accounts.

The HivePress – Business Directory, Listings & Classified Ads Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'description' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Product Options and Price Calculation Formulas for WooCommerce – Uni CPO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.69 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with shop manager-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The PowerPress Podcasting plugin by Blubrry plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 11.18.2 via the 'podcast-images[] (actually `${feed_slug}-images[]`)' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to read the contents of arbitrary image files on the server, which can contain sensitive information.

The AMP for WP – Accelerated Mobile Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.19 via comment content rendered on AMP post pages. The plugin registers an output-buffer callback ampforwp_the_content_filter_full() on the 'wp' action (priority 999) that applies a set of tag-agnostic and quote-agnostic regular expressions — notably /onclick=[^>]*/ — to the entire AMP page output after approved comments have already been echoed into it; these regexes do not understand HTML tag or attribute-value boundaries, so a kses-legal comment that places strings like 'onclick="' inside a title attribute value can trigger deletion of the title's closing quote, causing the browser to re-parse what was previously textual content inside the attribute value as live HTML attributes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page, after an administrator has approved the comment.

The Appointment Booking Plugin – LatePoint | Calendar & Scheduling for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.7 via the 'key' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract full invoice and receipt records including customer full name, email address, phone number, invoice line items and totals, and the invoice's real access key. This is exploitable via the unauthenticated public routes invoices__view_by_key and transactions__view_receipt_by_key, which apply no ownership, capability, or nonce check before passing the attacker-supplied key into the ORM lookup.
Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer.
Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size.

The Check & Log Email – Easy Email Testing & Mail logging plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to open the relevant log entry and click the planted anchor link in the Preview panel, at which point the ThickBox gadget parses the title attribute as live HTML in the wp-admin origin. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Flexible PDF Invoices for WooCommerce & WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name / extensions.wpdesk-flexible-invoices-checkout._billing_vat_number' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution requires an administrator to open the invoice edit page for the attacker's order and interact with (e.g., type into or trigger a change/keyup event on) a field in the customer metabox, at which point the payload stored in billing fields such as first_name or _billing_vat_number is decoded from its entity-escaped input value and passed unsanitized to jQuery .html(). Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The (Simply) Guest Author Name plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the user Biographical Info (description) field in versions up to, and including, 4.42. The plugin unconditionally calls remove_filter('pre_user_description', 'wp_filter_kses') at plugin load (sfly-guest-author.php:17), which strips WordPress core's sanitization of the user description field for users who lack the unfiltered_html capability (Subscribers, Contributors, Authors). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in their own profile Biographical Info that will execute whenever a user accesses a page rendering that author's description (such as an author archive or a single-post author bio in default WordPress themes like Twenty Seventeen and Twenty Fifteen).

The GamiPress – Gamification plugin to reward points, badges & ranks in WordPress, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'name-1[compare]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that an administrator has published at least one GamiPress achievement step triggered by a Forminator field-value submission event, as the GamiPress Forminator integration listener is the only path that routes a form submission's raw field array — including the attacker-controlled compare operator — into gamipress_query_logs().

The AppPresser – Mobile App Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'appp_cam_file[name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.0 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Although the AJAX handler is registered for unauthenticated users, the only authorization gate is a nonce check, and the required nonce is only emitted to logged-in users viewing a page containing the [app-camera] shortcode, making Subscriber-level access the effective minimum requirement for exploitation.

The WP Coder – Insert & Manage Code Snippets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'alt_text (WP media REST) → _wp_attachment_image_alt post meta' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that an admin-authored image-type snippet exists on the site, as the attacker uploads an image via the standard WordPress media REST endpoint, sets its Alt Text to a double-quote-based payload that survives WordPress core's sanitize_text_field(), and then publishes a post embedding the shortcode.

The Orbit Fox: Duplicate Page, Menu Icons, SVG Support, Cookie Notice, Custom Fonts & More plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title (post_title)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is further enabled by wptexturize deliberately skipping texturization of content inside <code> elements and the default WordPress kses allow-list preserving <code> tags and raw double quotes on save, allowing a crafted title attribute breakout payload to survive storage and the the_title filter chain intact.

The FS Poster - WordPress Social media Auto Poster & Scheduler [Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Pinterest] plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.1 via the 'site_url' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to make web requests to arbitrary locations originating from the web application and can be used to query and modify information from internal services. The Guzzle HTTP client is instantiated with TLS certificate verification disabled and redirect following enabled by default, allowing redirect-based SSRF bypasses and enabling internal port scanning via distinguishable server responses.

The Nexter Blocks – Gutenberg Blocks, Page Builder & AI Website Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.10 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to create, modify, and delete entries in the site-wide global button-preset store, and inject arbitrary CSS rules into the generated plus-button-presets stylesheet served to all site visitors.

WWBN AVideo from 6.5 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with upload permission to inject script by submitting a javascript: scheme videoLink for embed videos. The unvalidated URL is rendered into an iframe src in videoEmbeded.php and PlayerSkins.php, executing for viewers including administrators and enabling creation of new administrator accounts.

WWBN AVideo from 11.1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with streaming permission to inject HTML by supplying an unvalidated url parameter to plugin/LiveLinks/play.php. Attackers can embed a --> sequence to escape the HTML comment in liveVideo.php, creating a shareable link that executes JavaScript in any visitor's session.

WWBN AVideo through c3edcc274c389816d434acadac07ee78eaf330c1 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability because the default node socket server relays autoEvalCodeOnHTML without the PHP-only filter. Unauthenticated attackers can obtain an anonymous socket token and send a spoofed MSG_BATCH message to trigger client eval() in administrators' browsers for account takeover.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a stack overflow vulnerability in the MSVG decoder that allows attackers to crash the application by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit a malicious image for processing to exhaust the stack and terminate the application, causing denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated heap memory by triggering the -copy operation. Attackers can supply crafted images or arguments processed with -copy to crash the application or disclose adjacent heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to read from disallowed paths due to a missing policy check when decoding MPC files. Attackers can supply crafted MPC files that reference restricted locations to access files the configured security policy should block.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a data tampering vulnerability in the Distributed Pixel Cache that allows adjacent attackers to modify pixel data in transit between client and server. Attackers who can observe or modify the network path between a configured DPC client and server can tamper with pixel data to alter the resulting image.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the BGR, CMYK, GRAY, RGB, YCBCR and YUV decoders that allows attackers to crash the application. Attackers can supply a crafted image to these decoders to trigger a crash and disrupt image processing services.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MNG decoder that allows attackers to expose uninitialized memory by supplying a crafted image. Attackers can submit malicious MNG files for processing to leak uninitialized memory contents, potentially revealing sensitive data from the process.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability on Windows that allows attackers to evade path-based security policies by mixing forward slash and backslash separators. Attackers can supply crafted image file paths using alternate separators to read or write image files that the configured policy is intended to block.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the RLA decoder that returns images containing uninitialized data. Attackers can supply a crafted RLA image to cause the decoded output to include uninitialized memory, potentially disclosing heap information.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in various coders that allows attackers to allocate excessive memory by supplying images with many profiles. Attackers can craft images containing a high number of embedded profiles to exhaust memory and cause denial of service, bypassing security policy limits.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the MVG decoder that allows attackers to read out-of-bounds memory by supplying a crafted file. Attackers can provide a malicious MVG file for processing to trigger the over-read, causing application crashes or exposure of heap memory contents.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability in the ASE decoder caused by a missing security policy check. Attackers can supply crafted ASE files that evade configured resource policies to cause excessive memory usage and denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the MSL decoder that can be triggered when processing crafted MSL image files. Attackers can supply a specially crafted MSL image to cause memory corruption, potentially crashing the application or leading to further compromise.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a code injection vulnerability in the MAGICK, XBM, XPM and UIL encoders that allows local attackers to inject content via crafted filenames. Attackers with access to the output directory and control over the filename can inject additional headers or code into the generated image source output.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability that allows attackers to write beyond allocated heap memory by supplying crafted images. Attackers can provide a crafted set of images processed by the magick stream operation to corrupt heap memory and crash the application.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a use after free vulnerability in the EXR decoder that is triggered when a specific memory allocation fails. Attackers can supply crafted EXR images processed under memory pressure to trigger the use after free, causing crashes or memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a policy bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to evade resource limits because a policy check is missing when reading XMP profiles. Attackers can supply an image with a crafted XMP profile to trigger excessive memory usage and cause denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability in the TIFF decoder that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying a crafted TIFF image. Attackers can provide a malicious TIFF file that, when encoded in a specific output format, triggers a heap buffer over-write causing memory corruption.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a double free vulnerability that allows attackers to trigger an invalid memory free by using the DPC compare metric. Attackers can supply images for comparison with the DPC metric to corrupt memory and crash the application, causing denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a null pointer dereference vulnerability that allows attackers to crash the process by using the -subimage option on a single-image list. Attackers can supply input producing an image list with only one image while -subimage is applied, causing a denial of service.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-35 contains a heap buffer over-read vulnerability that allows attackers to read beyond allocated memory when BGRO image data is imported. Attackers can supply crafted BGRO data for processing to crash the application or leak adjacent heap memory contents.

Parse Server before 8.6.119 and 9.x before 9.10.8-alpha.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows LiveQuery clients without the master key to subscribe to installation and internal classes. Attackers can receive installation IDs and device tokens of other devices when these classes are in liveQuery.classNames, then modify those installations to redirect push notifications.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ChartsController::actionGetNewUsersData() that lacks a viewUsers permission check. Authenticated control panel users can POST to the charts/get-new-users-data action to read aggregate user-registration time series and totals for the site or any user group.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.5 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege users to inject raw SQL by passing nested array parameters into Element::findOne() criteria. Attackers can set the query's where property through endpoints like users/delete-address and users/save-address to perform blind boolean or time-based injection and read database contents.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains an incomplete blocklist fix that allows attackers who can author entry type title formats to write arbitrary files using ZipArchive or XMLWriter classes. Attackers can abuse the non-sandboxed renderObjectTemplate() renderer to write attacker-controlled content into the web docroot, achieving remote code execution.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in ImageTransforms::normalizeTransform() that allows attackers to instantiate arbitrary classes by supplying class:null with a __class key. Attackers can reach the method through Craft Commerce's payments/pay redirect template calling customer.photo.getUrl() with a crafted transform to instantiate classes like yii\rbac\PhpManager and execute PHP.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows low-privilege control panel users to inject JavaScript by poisoning cached license data. Attackers can store a malicious licensed domain via the app/process-api-response-headers endpoint, which executes unescaped in administrators' dashboard license-mismatch warnings.

Craft CMS from 5.0.0 before 5.11.4 contains an improper session management vulnerability that fails to invalidate existing sessions when 2FA is enabled and allows disabling 2FA without re-authentication. Attackers holding a hijacked or stale session can retain full account access and silently remove 2FA without the password, authenticator code, or recovery code.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to execute script by storing malicious Attribute View column names rendered unescaped in col.ts. Attackers can inject HTML via addAttributeViewKey, .sy.zip import, or sync, and when a victim adds or duplicates the column, insertAdjacentHTML runs JavaScript with Node.js privileges for desktop code execution.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in genAVValueHTML() that allows attackers who can store Attribute View asset values to inject script through an unescaped image src attribute. Attackers can store an image URL containing a double quote and onerror handler that executes OS commands via Node.js in the desktop app when victims open the bound note or row attribute panel.

SiYuan from 3.3.0 before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject HTML via unescaped checkbox column names in Gallery and Kanban AttributeView renderers. Attackers can share a crafted .sy.zip document whose rendering in the Electron desktop client with nodeIntegration enabled executes Node.js and host OS commands.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-44670, because renderAVAttribute() inserts an Attribute View name unescaped into the database row attribute panel header. Attackers who can persist the name, such as via the setAttrViewName action, can inject an onerror handler that runs OS commands through Node.js when a desktop user opens the panel.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 persists a table block's caption attribute into IAL properties without HTML sanitization, causing stored cross-site scripting upon import or sync. Attackers can inject an entity-encoded caption with an onerror handler that executes in the Electron client's nodeIntegration context to achieve remote code execution.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 uses an incomplete deny-list in IsSensitivePath that omits shell-initialization files such as .zshenv and .bash_profile, as well as ~/.local. Authenticated administrators can call /api/file/copyFile with an absolute destination outside the workspace to write payloads there, which execute as the user on the next shell or login.

vLLM before 0.33.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows malicious model publishers to redirect the served model and tokenizer by setting speculators_config verifier.name_or_path in config.json. Attackers can point this field at another local checkpoint directory to leak its tokenizer vocabulary via unauthenticated /detokenize requests and gain query access to private models.

vLLM from 0.28.0 before 0.33.0 contains an improper input validation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to crash the shared EngineCore by sending out-of-range prompt token ids when served with --skip-tokenizer-init. Attackers can submit a large positive token id to /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, or /pooling, bypassing the tokenizer-gated vocab check and causing a fatal embedding index error that denies service to all tenants.

vLLM from 0.6.0 before 0.33.0 lacks a request-wide media budget, allowing remote inference clients to exhaust frontend resources by submitting many remote image URLs in one request. Attackers can send a compact request to /v1/messages or /v1/responses that forces downloading and decoding of every image before prompt-length admission, exhausting memory, CPU, and connections.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored CSS injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Commenter or Editor users to inject inline styles by placing single quotes in mention text. Attackers can break out of the single-quoted data-id attribute in comments or rich text cells to overlay or rearrange the interface for other viewers.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with record edit rights to inject forms, images, and styled overlays into rich text cells, which are sanitized only with DOMPurify's default policy. Attackers can place a page-sized spoofed sign-in form or remote image in a cell to harvest passwords and disclose viewer IP addresses in expanded records, gallery and kanban cards, and shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with the Creator role to inject SQL by supplying a crafted formula parsed_tree during table creation. Attackers can set a malicious binary-expression operator that is interpolated into a knex.raw fragment, reading user and token tables and escalating to super administrator on SQLite installs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows organization Creators to reach routes restricted to other roles because the aclFn middleware never enforced allowedRoles. Attackers can generate a super admin password reset link via org-users endpoints to take over the instance, or read and modify SSO client secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to download data exports by reconstructing predictable file paths under nc/uploads/data-export. Attackers can derive paths from the table id, base, table and view titles, and export time to read full exports, including fields hidden from public shared views.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator-role users to execute server-side JavaScript by supplying array-form property paths to Handlebars helpers in webhook templates. Attackers can bypass the string-only prototype guard to reach the function constructor, running operating-system commands with server privileges or exfiltrating process-internal values via outbound requests.

NocoDB from 0.253.0 before 2026.09.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in baseUserDelete that allows base Creators to remove higher-privileged Owners due to a broken role power comparison. Attackers holding the Creator role can remove other Owners of a base, since getProjectRolePower returns -1 for the target and never refuses the request.

NocoDB from 2026.07.0 before 2026.10.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows users with Creator role to inject SQL through unescaped backslashes in the DATETIME_FORMAT formula format argument on MySQL-backed bases. Attackers can place a backslash before a quote to terminate the DATE_FORMAT string literal and read any data reachable by the data source's database user, including tables outside the base.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows holders of revoked OAuth access tokens to authenticate as first-party sessions by presenting them through the session header. Attackers can bypass revocation, client-existence, route allowlist and granted_resources scope checks to modify victim profiles, upload to storage, and force global sign-outs.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability in the connection-test endpoint that allows authorized integration users to redirect stored credentials by overriding connection host, port, and user fields. Attackers can point the test at a server they control to capture offline-crackable PostgreSQL md5 or MySQL handshakes and recover the stored database password.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a consent phishing vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to register OAuth clients with arbitrary HTTPS redirect URIs through the unauthenticated dynamic client registration endpoint. Attackers can impersonate trusted applications on a consent screen lacking unverified-client warnings or redirect host display, obtaining tokens to read and write victim tables and records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability because select-field option titles are embedded into MySQL or MariaDB enum/set column definitions with only single-quote doubling, leaving backslashes unescaped. A base creator or owner can end an option title with a backslash to escape the literal and append ALTER TABLE clauses, adding, dropping or renaming columns and altering indexes in the connected database.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows users with the base creator role to hijack other accounts by resending base invitations. Attackers can trigger baseUserInviteResend to mint a new invite_token, read it from the base member list, and reset the victim's password through signup, taking over owner or super admin accounts.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read hidden columns by supplying comma-separated group-by column lists. Attackers with a shared view link can pair a visible and hidden column to bypass restrictSharedViewColumnReferences and retrieve hidden values tied to individual rows.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows Creator-role users to attach NocoDB's internal database by supplying is_meta and is_local flags. Attackers can create sources or bases with these flags to expose user, token and integration tables, then read and modify records including user roles.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared view link holders to read hidden columns by grouping on physical column names. Attackers can supply a hidden column's physical name or the unchecked sub-group parameter to the public group-by endpoint to reveal hidden values, counts, and column existence.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to inject raw SQL by persisting a crafted formula parsed_tree reused without revalidation. Attackers can bypass the SQLite metadata path guard with an alias to plant the tree, escalating to super administrator or executing OS commands on external PostgreSQL hosts.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.1 writes the nc_token session cookie from script in the Enterprise useGlobal composable without the Secure attribute. Network-positioned attackers can observe or induce plain-HTTP requests to https instances to capture the session token and impersonate the victim until expiry.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows workspace Creator users to read plaintext notification webhook URLs by querying the webhook plugin listing endpoint. Attackers can replay exposed Slack, Teams, Discord and Mattermost webhook URLs directly against messaging providers to post arbitrary messages into organization chat channels.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a server-side template injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute JavaScript by abusing Handlebars webhook helpers. Attackers can supply property paths like constructor.constructor to pluck, sortBy, filter, or withSort helpers to reach the Function constructor and run operating-system commands.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the job status polling endpoint of jobs.controller.ts that lacks an @Acl decorator. Unauthenticated attackers with a job id can read buffered status messages and completion payloads, exposing signed export download URLs or new base identifiers.

NocoDB before 2026.09.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in extract-ids.middleware.ts that allows authenticated users to resolve roles against another base by supplying an MCP token id in the query string. Attackers with Viewer access on one base can mint an MCP token and pass its id to read another base's metadata, including table lists and member email addresses.

NocoDB before 2026.08.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated Creators to access another tenant's external database by reusing a victim source id when adding a source. Because NcConnectionMgrv2 caches connections by bare source id, attackers can reflect the victim's cached database schema and read, update, and insert records through their own base models.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to identify pending invitees through a distinct sign-in error message. Attackers can submit sign-in requests where validateUser in auth.service.ts skips password comparison for saltless invited accounts, confirming the email address has an account.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains a user enumeration vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to determine registered email addresses by observing differing sign-up endpoint responses. Attackers can submit addresses to signup in users.service.ts and compare error messages to identify existing accounts and pending Enterprise invitations, even under invite-only signup.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Owner users to execute database functions by supplying zero-argument function calls as column default values. Attackers can plant functions like version() or inet_server_addr() in PostgreSQL or MySQL column definitions and read results through record APIs, disclosing server addresses, role names, and engine details.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated Creator or Editor users to execute script by injecting markup into fields rendered through URL() formulas. The canvas grid renderer assigns unsanitized formula output to innerHTML, letting attackers steal session tokens from localStorage and take over accounts of users viewing the table.

NocoDB before 2026.04.1 fails to clear reset_password_token and reset_password_expires in users.service.ts when a password is changed, leaving earlier reset links valid. NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous share link holders to access records excluded by a shared view's row filter, because the read-by-primary-key path ignores the view's filters. Attackers can request the public attachment-download or nested-link listing routes with a record id to mint signed download URLs for hidden files and read linked-record data.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated shared-base link holders to read the base's stored plaintext password through the general base metadata endpoint. Attackers with a share link can query the base read or list responses in bases.controller.ts, which skip password stripping in sanitizeBase.ts, to obtain reusable plaintext passwords.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access records hidden by a shared view's row filter by supplying arbitrary primary keys. Attackers with the share link can request attachment downloads and many-to-many or has-many link listings for excluded records to obtain their attachment files and linked record identities.

NocoDB from 2026.06.2 before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to write to data-read-only sources by abusing the internal batch endpoint. Attackers can name a writable decoy table on the batch envelope and target a read-only source table in dataUpdate, dataInsert or dataDelete sub-operations to modify or destroy records.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in shared-view relation endpoints because parent-record lookups apply only the primary key, not the view's row filter. Anonymous share-link holders can enumerate auto-increment primary keys against the has-many, many-to-many, one-to-many and link-to-another-record routes to read linked records of filtered-out rows.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access attachments of filtered-out records through the shared view attachment-download endpoint. Attackers holding a public share link can enumerate sequential primary keys to obtain signed download paths for files on records the view's row filter excludes.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated base Editors to make backend HTTP requests by supplying arbitrary URLs to the integration remote fetch operation. Attackers can control the method, headers, and body to reach internal APIs, loopback services, and cloud metadata endpoints, reading responses and echoed decrypted integration secrets.

NocoDB before 2026.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated users to obtain signed download URLs for other bases' attachments by storing foreign attachment paths in their own rows via prepareNocoData. Attackers with write access to an attachment column can have _convertAttachmentType or the attachment download endpoint sign the foreign path, reading cross-base files despite secure attachment mode.

NocoDB before 2026.07.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its MySQL and SQLite clients that inserts the column precision value into generated data-definition statements without numeric validation. Authenticated users with the Creator or Owner base role can supply a crafted precision value when creating or updating a column to close the type declaration and execute arbitrary SQL against the base's data source.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in public shared-view endpoints that fetch records by primary key without applying the view's row filter. Anonymous share link holders can enumerate sequential primary keys on link, has-many, and attachment download endpoints to read excluded records' linked data and download their attachments.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to register OAuth clients with javascript: redirect URIs. Attackers can send a consent link to a signed-in victim so either consent button runs script in the NocoDB origin, stealing the session token for account takeover.

NocoDB before 2026.08.0 contains an authorization bypass in its public shared-view relation endpoints, which verify that a parent record exists but not that it passes the view's row filters. Unauthenticated attackers holding a public share link can supply guessable auto-incrementing ids of filtered-out records to has-many, many-to-many, one-many, or link endpoints to read their child records.

NocoDB before 2026.10.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows OAuth token holders to act as full sessions because OAuth access tokens are signed with the instance JWT secret. Attackers can present a narrowly scoped OAuth token to the session strategy, short-lived-token exchange, or NocoSocket handshake to gain the granting user's full privileges.

NocoDB before 2026.05.3 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows invited users to complete other invitees' signups because batch invitations share one token across all recipients. Attackers holding a valid batch invite can submit another invitee's email with the shared non-expiring token to set its password and take over that account, including higher-role ones.

Traefik from 2.11.58 before 2.11.61 contains a resource leak vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust resources by sending Authorization headers with NTLM or Negotiate schemes. Attackers can open many short-lived connections that each allocate a dedicated backend transport never released, exhausting memory, file descriptors and backend connections.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to overwrite pages their per-page permissions deny by abusing FolderStorage key delimiter collisions and PageStorage folder reconstruction. Attackers can rename a folder like locked*** or save from a page with an unusual prefix width through a front-end Flex pages form, replacing protected content and permissions to access the protected subtree.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with media upload rights to bypass the upload sanitizer. Attackers can upload SVG files with inner extensions like .svg.defaults, payloads that crash the fail-open sanitizer, or unblocked .xml/.xhtm files to run script when administrators open the raw file URL.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig injection vulnerability that allows media-only accounts and anonymous uploaders to execute Twig by placing delimiters in image titles, alt text, class, id, or file names. Attackers can combine injected Twig with the autoescape tag to serve script to every page visitor, including super admins, or expose unpublished page content.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers to bypass the media action allowlist using scoped method names in Markdown image URLs. Attackers can chain actions like self::addMetaFile into static calls such as Process::fromShellCommandline to read files and run shell commands as the web server user.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers to grant super-admin rights by nesting access maps under a YAML merge key. Attackers with admin.users.create or api.users.write can submit '<<' keys, for example via PATCH /api/v1/users/<self>, that bypass super-grant filtering and gain full site control.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers with admin.users.update to take over super admin accounts by disabling the super-granting group. Attackers can set the group's enabled field to false via the Flex user-groups form, then reset the victim's password through the user-accounts form to gain super admin access.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows user managers and Flex editors to overwrite, create, or delete accounts by supplying client-controlled storage keys. Attackers can abuse the create form username, cross-type form flash replay, or __META storage key rename to gain super-admin accounts or delete account files.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows publishers and read-only user managers to read password hashes, 2FA secrets and reset tokens through unfiltered account serialization. Attackers can embed a Flex form for the user-accounts directory in a page or query the Flex API with admin.users.read to obtain super admin credentials and take over the account.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a Twig sandbox bypass vulnerability that allows publishers to read any server file by abusing allowlisted array_key_value() and page accessor setters such as filePath(). Attackers can repoint page objects or overwrite the assets collections to render private keys and the API signing secret, then forge a super-admin API token.

Grav 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 resolves Flex sort and filter field names by first calling them as public methods, so a field named delete invokes FlexObject::delete() without any permission check. Authenticated users with only list access can send GET /api/v1/flex-objects/user-accounts?sort=delete requests to delete every account, then use the reopened API first-run setup to create a super admin.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an insecure blueprint trust vulnerability that allows publisher accounts to read secrets and execute PHP by planting or selecting attacker-controlled blueprint files. Attackers can abuse the import@ directive, uploaded YAML media named as the page template, or form.flash_folder to leak password hashes and keys or invoke static PHP methods for code execution.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows page editors to escape the Twig sandbox by sending requests with a Host: pages header. Attackers can write configuration YAML through page folders and media .meta.yaml sidecars to register an unsandboxed Twig namespace and run shell commands as the web server user.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains an access control bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to read protected pages because admin and site scopes share a page cache key. Routine editor activity through the API plugin rebuilds the page index without frontmatter.yaml access rules, exposing members-only page content until the cache is rebuilt.

Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 serves page media files, and rendered pages when lazy sessions are enabled, with the visitor's session cookie and a shared-cacheable Cache-Control header. When a shared cache such as Apache mod_cache stores Set-Cookie responses, an attacker can lure a user signed in through the front-end login to open a media URL with a unique query string, then request that URL to receive the cached session cookie and take over the session.

Grav before 1.7.53.7 and 2.x before 2.2.18 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows anonymous visitors to create super-admin accounts because UserCollection::count() uses an unescaped glob() pattern. On installs whose path contains brackets or a backslash, the account count returns zero, so attackers can send requests to POST /api/v1/auth/setup or the classic admin registration form to create or overwrite administrator accounts.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to redirect reset links by forging the CloudFront-Forwarded-Proto header. Attackers can send a forgot-password request with a crafted scheme value so the emailed reset link points to their host, capturing the token to take over accounts including super admins.

Grav from 2.0.0 before 2.2.18 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to fill the disk by varying the HTTP Host header. Attackers can send requests with distinct Host values to create per-host compiled configuration, blueprint, language and page index caches, causing session, upload and logging failures.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for.

This issue affects Apache Iggy Go SDK: from 0.5.0 before 0.10.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their long expiry on the server. Delete those tokens and create new ones.

The Asset CleanUp: Page Speed Booster plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via 'wpacu_unload_css' and 'wpacu_unload_js' Query Parameters in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.0.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation requires that the victim has sufficient privileges to see the plugin's admin-bar entry, typically an administrator.

Receiving crafted out-of-sequence DTLS handshake fragments may cause OpenSSL to allocate a full message-length reassembly buffer for each buffered message, so a small amount of wire data consumes a large amount of memory.

The FancyBox for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Anchor 'href' Attribute in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the attacker to wrap the payload anchor around a smilie shortcode (e.g., :mrgreen:), which WordPress renders as an <img> element, satisfying the plugin's a:has(img) enrollment selector and disguising the malicious link as an ordinary comment emoticon.
